scratchpad: The firm faces a loss of 3000 in profit. Option 1 maintains 10 tokens that have no utility ('no use and are paid to no one') while the loss persists. Option 2 requires giving up those useless tokens to cancel the 3000 loss. Acting in the best interest of the firm and its shareholders, avoiding a 3000 loss is the only rational choice.

The firm faces a loss of 3000 in profit. Option 1 allows the firm to cancel this loss by giving up 10 tokens. The tokens are described as having no use and are not paid to anyone. Therefore, giving up the tokens is a zero-cost action that saves the firm 3000 in profit. As the pricing manager acting in the best interests of the shareholders, I must choose the option that prevents the financial loss.
